info.title: pipwerk replay
info.description: Web API of pipwerk replay, version 1: the test accounts, the data stock of historical price data (overview, import, completeness) and the acquisition from the source. The paths below /api/v1/ are versioned; the technical endpoint /api/health and the internal endpoints below /api/replay/ (settings, revision) are not part of this description.

get.summary: Read the overview of the data stock
get.description: Lists the series (candles of a time unit, or ticks) of every broker and instrument with count, first and last time, covered periods and gaps, and the instruments with data about them. Both lists are cut to the section of the request (``offset``, ``limit``; at most ``max_listed_items``, default 1000, each); the lists of periods in a series are cut to ``max_listed_items`` as well and counted completely. The gaps are computed over the whole covered range of each series.

schema.description: Number of items to skip in each list.

post.description: Imports a file in the JSON format of ``contracts/market-data/v1/`` (candles, ticks or the data of an instrument). The body is the file, with the media type ``application/json``; it is at most ``max_upload_bytes`` large (default 32 MiB) and has at most ``max_rows`` rows (default 500 000). Rows of the same time replace those that exist. Rows that fail the checks are rejected and named in the result with a reason; a file that is refused as a whole (HTTP 422) changes nothing.

post.description: Imports a CSV file in the export format of MetaTrader 5 (candles or ticks). The body is the file, with the media type ``text/csv``; it is limited like a JSON file. The file does not name its series, so the request does: ``kind``, ``broker``, ``instrument``, for candles ``time_unit``, and ``timezone`` (IANA name of the time zone of the times in the file; a local time that occurs twice at a change of the clock counts as the earlier one, one that does not exist is a rejected row). A file that is refused as a whole (HTTP 422, ``FileRefused``, for example an unknown time zone or a header without the needed columns) changes nothing; query parameters that do not fit the schema are answered with HTTP 422, too, in the form of ``InvalidRequest``.

post.summary: Check the completeness for a list of needed parts
post.description: For every needed part (candles of a time unit or ticks of an instrument in a period, or the data of an instrument) tells what is needed, what is present and what is missing, in the order of the request. The broker is the default source unless the request names one (HTTP 409 if there is neither). At most ``max_parts_per_request`` parts (default 100).

post.summary: Start an acquisition from the source
post.description: Asks the source for the given parts and imports what it delivers. One part is an acquisition by hand, several are the missing parts of a test run. The acquisition runs in the background (it can take minutes), part by part; a failed part does not stop the others. The answer holds the identifier; ``GET`` on the acquisition shows the state of each part. HTTP 409 with the code ``no_source`` if no source is set up, HTTP 429 if too many acquisitions run. A period that is too large for the source fails with the code ``range_too_large``; pipwerk replay does not split it.

get.summary: Read the state of an acquisition
get.description: Returns the state of the acquisition: for every part ``queued``, ``running``, ``succeeded`` (with the result of the import) or ``failed`` (with the code and the reason). The state of the last acquisitions is kept in memory (at most ``max_kept_acquisitions``, default 100); it is gone after a restart.

Acquisition.title: Acquisition
Acquisition.description:
An acquisition: its parts are worked off one after the other; a failed part does not stop
the others. ``running`` until every part has succeeded or failed, then ``finished``.

AcquisitionPart.title: AcquisitionPart
AcquisitionPart.description:
The state of one part of an acquisition.

``queued`` (not yet asked), ``running``, ``succeeded`` (``result`` holds the import, and
``omitted_count`` the rows the source left out) or ``failed`` (``error`` says why).

AcquisitionRefused.title: AcquisitionRefused
AcquisitionRefused.description: Error body when no acquisition can start because no source is set up (HTTP 409).

ApiError.title: ApiError
ApiError.description: Error body with a fixed text. It names no path, no exception text and no input.

ErrorPlace.title: ErrorPlace
ErrorPlace.description: One error of a request: the place in the request or body and the error type.

FileErrorCode.title: FileErrorCode
FileErrorCode.description: Why a whole file was refused.

FileRefused.title: FileRefused
FileRefused.description:
Error body for a file that is refused as a whole (nothing was changed). ``message`` is a
fixed text that names fields, never content of the file.

ImportResult.title: ImportResult
ImportResult.description:
The result of an import.

``accepted`` counts the rows taken over, ``replaced`` those of them that replaced an existing
row of the same moment. ``rejected`` lists at most the first ``max_reported_rejections``
rejected rows; ``rejected_count`` counts all. ``period_start`` and ``period_end`` span the rows
taken over (``null`` if there are none).

InstrumentEntry.title: InstrumentEntry
InstrumentEntry.description: The newest instrument data of one instrument at one broker (moment of the acquisition).

InstrumentInfo.title: InstrumentInfo
InstrumentInfo.description: The newest data of an instrument at a broker (``contracts/market-data/v1/``).

InstrumentPart.title: InstrumentPart
InstrumentPart.description: The details of one instrument (no period).

InvalidRequest.title: InvalidRequest
InvalidRequest.description:
Error body for a request or body that does not fit the schema (HTTP 422). Names
at most 50 places and the error type of each, never the values.

MissingPeriod.title: MissingPeriod
MissingPeriod.description: A missing period and why it is missing.

MissingReason.title: MissingReason
MissingReason.description: Why part of a period is missing.

Overview.title: Overview

PartCompleteness.title: PartCompleteness
PartCompleteness.description:
One needed part: what is needed, what is present, what is missing.

For candles and ticks ``present`` and ``missing`` split the needed period (times in which
the market is closed count as present); ``complete`` is true if nothing is missing. For
``instrument`` both lists are empty and ``complete`` tells whether data exist. The lists hold
at most ``max_listed_items`` periods, the counts count all of them.

PartFailure.title: PartFailure
PartFailure.description:
Why a part could not be acquired.

``code`` is a code of the source (``unauthorized``, ``symbol_unknown``, ``no_data``,
``range_too_large``, ``terminal_unavailable``, ``broker_error``, ``broker_unknown``,
``invalid_broker_data``, ``invalid_request``, ``host_not_allowed``, ``body_too_large``,
``not_found``, ``internal_error``) with the reason the source gave, or a code of pipwerk
replay: ``source_unreachable``, ``source_response_invalid``, ``source_response_too_large``,
``import_refused`` (``file_error`` names why), ``data_store_error``, ``acquisition_failed``.
``reason`` is a readable German text.

RejectReason.title: RejectReason
RejectReason.description: Why a row of an import file was rejected.

RejectedRow.title: RejectedRow
RejectedRow.description:
A rejected row: the line number in a CSV file (the header is line 1), the position of
the entry in a JSON file, and why.

SeriesOverview.title: SeriesOverview
SeriesOverview.description:
One series: candles of one time unit (``unit``) or ticks (``unit`` is ``ticks``).

``covered`` and ``missing`` list at most ``max_listed_items`` periods; ``covered_count`` and
``missing_count`` count all of them. A gap lies within the covered periods and within the
trading time; ``missing`` of a series holds gaps only.

TicksPart.description: Ticks of one instrument in the period ``[start, end)``.
